bihar_raw_news.title: From Bihar to Punjab: How ChatGPT led elderly man home - The Siasat Daily
bihar_raw_news.content: ChatGPT interface on a computer screen. Photo: Emiliano Vittoriosi/Unsplash A four-day search across state lines ended in an unexpected reunion after an elderly Punjab pilgrim, who disappeared while on a state-sponsored trip to Amritsar, turned up hundreds of kilometres away in Bihar, where a stranger sheltered him and tracked down his family with the help of online searches, reports said on Sunday, September 20. Under the Punjab government’s Mukh Mantri Tirath Yatra scheme, Chaman Lal of Fatehgarh Gujran village in Ludhiana travelled to Amritsar on September 11 to visit the Golden Temple. However, he got separated from the group and wandered to Amritsar railway station, his family said. The elderly man has struggled with memory-related issues. From there, it turns out, Lal boarded a train heading to Bihar and travelled to Gaya, more than 1,200 kilometres from home. In Gaya, Neeraj noticed Lal wandering and asking for food. According to Neeraj, while Lal could not recall his address, “He could only remember the name of his village, Fatehgarh Gujran.” Speaking to The Statesman , Neeraj said he took Lal home to stay while he tried to find the elderly man’s village. Three days of research on ChatGPT Since Lal was speaking Punjabi, that helped Neeraj narrow down his search to that state. He used ChatGPT and other internet searches to identify Fatehgarh Gujran as a village near Machhiwara Sahib in Ludhiana. A three-day search was all it took. Neeraj then accompanied Lal from Gaya to Ludhiana and then to Machhiwara, where he showed his photograph to locals on Saturday. Local man Master Krishan Lal recognised Lal from a missing-person photograph circulated on social media and contacted his grandson, Sukhchain Singh. Singh then reached Machhiwara and was reunited with his grandfather. “We searched for him in Amritsar but could not find him. I am extremely thankful to Neeraj for keeping my grandfather safe and bringing him back,” Singh was quoted as saying. Meanwhile, for Neeraj, this isn’t new; the construction sector employee in Gaya has been helping people in distress since his school days. “When I saw him alone at the station, I felt I should help him,” he said. bihar_raw_news.title: CM Samrat Chaudhory calls for everyone's participation in building a prosperous Bihar
bihar_raw_news.content: CM Samrat Chaudhory calls for everyone's participation in building a prosperous Bihar ANI | Updated: Sep 20, 2026 19:43 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel Patna ( Bihar ) [ India ], September 20 (ANI): Chief Minister Samrat Chaudhory inaugurated the 'Viksit Bihar : Foundation to Construction' (Viksit Bihar : Neev se Nirman tak) brainstorming session and 'Lav-Kush Pratibha Samman Samaroh' (Talent Felicitation Ceremony) by lighting the ceremonial lamp at the Bapu Sabhagar within the Samrat Ashok Convention Centre. Talented individuals who excelled in various fields were honoured at the event, which was organised by the Progressive Intellectuals Association, Bihar . According to the Chief Minister's Office, the Chief Minister stated that the foundation of unity for the Lav-Kush community was laid in 1994, and this unity remains intact today. He emphasised that the Lav-Kush community is not against anyone; rather, it seeks to play its role in the prosperity of Bihar and the development of the nation while moving forward with a commitment to justice. Following the 'Kurmi Chetna Rally' and 'Kushwaha Sammelan' in 1992-93, both communities jointly organised the 'Lav-Kush Sammelan' in 1994. He extended his congratulations to all the leaders who initiated this movement. He noted that this social unity subsequently took on a political form and played a crucial role in advancing the political parties associated with it. “Today is the time to realise the vision of a developed India and a prosperous Bihar . Prime Minister Narendra Modi has envisioned a developed India , while former Chief Minister of Bihar Nitish Kumar has envisioned a prosperous Bihar ; we are working to turn these visions into reality,” he said. The Chief Minister remarked that Bihar possesses a glorious history. Great rulers like Chandragupta Maurya and Emperor Ashoka provided direction to India and the world from this very land. There is a need to present Bihar 's historical and cultural heritage to the world with greater emphasis. He noted that significant changes have occurred in Bihar 's economy and infrastructure since 2005. At the time of the bifurcation of Bihar and Jharkhand, Bihar 's economy was largely dependent on revenue generated from Jharkhand; however, today, Bihar 's budget has far surpassed that of Jharkhand. He noted that in 2024, while Jharkhand presented a budget of Rs 1.39 lakh crore, Bihar presented a budget of Rs 3.17 lakh crore. The Chief Minister stated that academic sessions commenced simultaneously in 211 degree colleges across Bihar on July 15. Additionally, 700 model schools (Saraswati Vidya Niketan) have been established, catering to 3.5 lakh students. He mentioned that 75,000 teachers have been connected via the 'Vidyarthi Saathi' app, enabling a large number of students to access online education even at night; currently, approximately 1.42 lakh children are studying through this app during night hours. He highlighted that work is underway to develop a grand corridor in Bodh Gaya. bihar_raw_news.content: IANS RJD National Working President and Bihar Leader of Opposition Tejashwi Yadav has criticised the BJP’s plan to observe Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s birthday with an ‘Aashirwad Ka Diya’ campaign, citing the ongoing flood crisis in the state. Patna: RJD national working president Tejashwi Yadav on Sunday alleged that while the Bihar government's "coffers were empty", crores were spent on the birthday celebrations of Prime Minister Narendra Modi . Speaking to reporters here, Yadav, the leader of the opposition in the state assembly, attacked the government over the handling of the flood situation in the state, demanding to know why the calamity has not been declared as a 'national disaster'. He also demanded that the state government provide Rs 15,000 as immediate relief to every drought and flood-hit family in the state. bihar_raw_news.title: Jan Suraaj announces candidates for 5 Bihar Legislative Council seats
bihar_raw_news.content: Jan Suraaj Party founder Prashant Kishor Prashant Kishor-led Jan Suraaj Party (JSP) on Sunday announced candidates for five Bihar Legislative Council constituencies, getting an early start on elections to eight graduates’ and teachers’ seats that are expected to be announced soon. The terms of members representing the eight constituencies — four graduates’ and four teachers’ seats — are due to expire in November. Jan Suraaj has already said it plans to contest all eight seats as part of its organisational expansion in Bihar. Announcing the candidates at a press conference, Kishor said Afaq Ahmed would seek re-election from the Saran teachers’ constituency. Ahmed had won the seat six years ago with Kishor’s support, before the former poll strategist launched Jan Suraaj as a political party. Divya Jyoti, a lawyer and academician-turned-politician who joined Jan Suraaj last week, will contest from the Patna teachers’ constituency. The seat is currently held by JD(U) chief spokesperson Neeraj Kumar. The party has named S P Rai as its candidate from the Darbhanga teachers’ constituency, while Ravindra Yadav will contest the Darbhanga graduates’ seat. Rajnish Ranjan has been fielded from the Kosi graduates’ constituency. Live Events The Legislative Council election is separate from the Bihar Assembly polls and will cover graduates’ and teachers’ constituencies spread across around 30 districts of the state. Unlike Assembly elections, the contests are decided by specialised electorates comprising eligible graduates and teachers. Candidates’ local influence, their standing among these voters and the organisational strength of their parties are expected to play an important role in the eight contests. With five candidates now declared, Jan Suraaj has three more nominees to announce if it goes ahead with its plan to contest all eight seats. Add as a Reliable and Trusted News Source Add Now! bihar_raw_news.title: Why Bihar is investing big infra in Gaya's sacred geography - India Today
bihar_raw_news.content: SIGN IN Edition IN IN US Download App Follow Us On: News India Today Insight Why Bihar is investing big infra in Gaya’s sacred geography Get 37% off on an annual Print + Digital subscription of India Today Magazine SUBSCRIBE Why Bihar is investing big infra in Gaya's sacred geography The revamp of the Vishnupad Temple precinct along Kashi Vishwanath Corridor lines and Son-Falgu river-linking, costing Rs 3,516 crore, aim for a durable pilgrimage economy Advertisement Amitabh Srivastava UPDATED: Sep 20, 2026 16:57 IST Edited By: Ashish Mukherjee Bihar’s Samrat Choudhary government, on September 15, put Gaya on the fast track to development, approving a Rs 3,516 crore package that brings together two seemingly unrelated projects. One is the Rs 2,520 crore redevelopment of the Vishnupad Temple precinct on the lines of Varanasi’s Kashi Vishwanath Corridor. The other is a Rs 996.05 crore project to link the Son and Falgu rivers. advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story Taken together, the two projects point to a larger ambition: if Gayaji is already one of Bihar’s biggest religious-tourism destinations, its infrastructure must keep pace with the scale of its pilgrimage economy. That means not only upgrading the spaces around its sacred sites but also addressing the water challenge that has long shaped the Falgu. The September 15 cabinet approval is part of Choudhary’s broader push to develop Bihar’s religious-tourism centres and give them infrastructure commensurate with their growing significance. Gaya is one of the few places in the state that draw a great number of Indian pilgrims and foreign visitors. Provisional Bihar tourism figures for January to July 2026 put domestic tourist visits to Gaya at 1.14 million; alongside are 96,465 foreign visitors. This is in addition to the footfalls recorded at Bodh Gaya, where another 1.46 million domestic visitors and 134,000 foreign visitors were recorded in the same period. Together, the two destinations accounted for about 231,000 foreign visitors in the first seven months of the year. The scale becomes more striking when placed against the state capital. Patna recorded only 6,429 foreign visitors in the same seven-month period, according to the provisional figures. In other words, the Gaya-Bodh Gaya belt is the state’s principal meeting point between two very different streams of religious travel—Hindu pilgrimage at Gaya and global Buddhist pilgrimage at Bodh Gaya. And even those numbers understate the annual load. The January-July figures do not capture the Pitripaksha Mela, which falls in September-October. That is when Vishnupad, the Falgu ghats and the city’s pind daan economy get their biggest annual rush. The government's Vishnupad plan reads almost like a response to that pressure: multi-level parking, elevated pathways, ghats, bridges, ramps, dormitories, a canteen, pedestrian infrastructure and public amenities are all part of the package. The project will be implemented by the Bihar State Road Development Corporation. national_raw_news.content: Rashtriya Sankalp Samaroh is being organized at various locations in the country to eradicate drug abuse among youth as part of Nasha Mukt Yuva Abhiyan. The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports has said that Rashtriya Sankalp Samaroh is being organised across 1,067 locations in the country. The Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat- 100 Weeks Nasha Mukt Yuva Abhiyan is witnessing nationwide youth mobilisation. The Ministry added that this programme will be organised across 471 District MY Bharat Offices, along with 596 locations of partner organisations. The Samaroh aims to bring the campaign’s message directly to young people through Nasha Mukt Pledge, Signature Campaign, thematic street plays, slogan writing and youth-led discussions. As part of the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyan, several special programmes are being organised across Telangana. Social and voluntary organisations, is participating in this campaign. As part of this initiative, a cycling rally was organised today in Hyderabad with the aim of freeing the youth from the clutches of drugs. As part of the nationwide call, Nasha Mukt Bharat Cycling Ride organised today on Necklace Road, Hyderabad. BJP Rajya Sabha MP Dr. K. Laxman took part in the rally, cycling alongside youth and cyclists along Necklace Road. Highlighting the severe impact of drugs on the youth, he administered a pledge to the participants. Speaking on the occasion, MP Laxman said a healthy youth is the foundation for building a strong Viksit Bharat, and called upon everyone to join this movement. The event created renewed awareness among youth for a drug-free society.

national_raw_news.title: Union Sports Minister Mandaviya leads Indian diaspora at 'Sundays on Cycle' in Nagoya to ...
national_raw_news.content: Union Sports Minister Mandaviya leads Indian diaspora at 'Sundays on Cycle' in Nagoya to Cheer for Bharat Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर Union Sports Minister Mandaviya leads Indian diaspora at 'Sundays on Cycle' in Nagoya to Cheer for Bharat ANI | Updated: Sep 20, 2026 14:06 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel Aichi-Nagoya [Japan], September 20 (ANI): Union Minister of Youth Affairs & Sports Mansukh Mandaviya led the 91st edition of ‘Sundays on Cycle’ at Meijo Park in Nagoya, Japan, on Sunday, September 20, 2026, where he rallied together members of the Indian diaspora to extend support and encouragement to the Indian contingent participating in the Asian Games 2026. The initiative reflected the Government of India's continued efforts to strengthen people-to-people connect with the Indian diaspora through the universal language of sports, while reinforcing the message of fitness and healthy living under the Fit India Movement, as per a press release from the Union Sports Ministry. Mandaviya interacted with participants of the 91st Sundays on Cycle event and appreciated their enthusiasm for coming together to support Team India in the Asian Games. The Indian community in Nagoya came together through ‘Sundays on Cycle’ to ‘Cheer for Bharat’ and boost the morale of the athletes participating on the biggest continental stage. “The Asian Games have commenced in Nagoya, Japan, and we have a contingent of over 500 young athletes from India, who are participating in the Games,” said Dr Mandaviya. “The Indian diaspora in Nagoya has shown great enthusiasm to support and cheer our athletes by joining the Sundays on Cycle event here,” he said. “I am happy to say that our contingent is performing well, and our diaspora is working hard to boost their morale," he added. Mandaviya is in Nagoya, Japan, for the Asian Games 2026, where he is interacting with Indian athletes, officials, and members of the Indian diaspora, underscoring the Government's sustained efforts towards promoting sports excellence and a fitter, healthier India on the global stage. Fit India Sundays on Cycle is organised by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports (MYAS) in collaboration with the Cycling Federation of India (CFI), Raahgiri Foundation and MY Bharat. The cycling drive is conducted simultaneously across all States and Union Territories, including at SAI Regional Centres, National Centres of Excellence (NCOEs), SAI Training Centres (STCs), Khelo India State Centres of Excellence (KISCEs) and Khelo India Centres (KICs). Over 6000 NAMO Fit India clubs also organise the cycling initiative nationwide every week. national_raw_news.title: Three-Day IAF Air Show To Be Held In Varanasi In October, PM Modi Likely To Attend
national_raw_news.content: Varanasi Gears Up For Three-Day IAF Air Show Over Ganga, PM Modi Likely To Attend States Three-Day IAF Air Show To Be Held In Varanasi In October, PM Modi Likely To Attend Swarajya Staff Sep 20, 2026 | Updated 12:27 PM GMT+5:30 Save & read from anywhere! Bookmark stories for easy access on any device or the Swarajya app . Sign In Prefer Prefer Three IAF Rafales flying in formation. (Via PIB) Varanasi is set to witness its first-ever air show as the Indian Air Force (IAF) prepares to stage a spectacular three-day aerial display over the sacred Ganges. Scheduled for 22, 23 and 25 October, the event is expected to draw crowds of 20 lakh people to witness fighter jets and helicopters performing above the historic ghats stretching from Namo Ghat to Assi Ghat. The Indian Air Force plans to deploy more than three dozen aircraft for the show, including Rafale fighter jets, the renowned Suryakiran aerobatic team, Rudra helicopters, C-295 aircraft, Tejas fighters and Dakota aircraft. Performances will take place between noon and 2pm each day, with displays lasting approximately 90 minutes as three to five aircraft showcase aerial manoeuvres simultaneously over the river. Prime Minister Narendra Modi is expected to attend as chief guest on the final day, with Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and senior military officials also likely to participate. Air Force authorities have coordinated extensively with Lal Bahadur Shastri International Airport officials, with Suryakiran jets taking off from Varanasi Airport whilst other aircraft will fly from surrounding districts. District administration has begun preparations to manage the anticipated crowds, with special arrangements being made across 84 ghats along the riverfront. Namo Ghat, designated as the main control centre, will be handed over to Air Force control from 16 October, with public access restricted during the setup period. Officials have enlisted support from neighbouring Chandauli, Ghazipur and Jaunpur districts to handle crowd management and security. Rehearsals for the historic event will commence on 20 October and continue through 22 October. The Rajghat bridge and boat services on the Ganges will remain closed during performances for safety reasons. Local authorities are preparing for crowds comparable to the Dev Deepavali festival, with arrangements for approximately 5,000 VIP guests from across India and abroad.
